recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if the work group wants new general guidance on when local CodeSystem resources are appropriate; that would be a new CodeSystem/terminology policy issue rather than a missing application of this DSTU1 ValueSet request.
issue_request: FHIR-5378 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 vocab change request for ValueSet section 6.22.1 asking that wording about value sets defining their own inline code systems explicitly mention limited-scope/local-value appropriateness or otherwise explain the rationale.
initial_application: No Jira-keyed implementation commit was found. Historical commit ab6d7c95d1 added the old ValueSet prose saying inline code-system definitions were for small, simple code systems found throughout an implementation context and not for large public terminologies; Jira comments recorded that Grahame had added this text because of other tasks. Commit 886ad6667c then preserved the guidance while renaming ValueSet.define to ValueSet.codeSystem.
additional_context: The current specification no longer supports ValueSet inline code systems. Commit 1120eb61d0 removed inline-code-system language and examples as part of the ValueSet/CodeSystem split. Current ValueSet source says a ValueSet draws codes from one or more CodeSystem definitions for use in a particular context, while current terminology guidance explains locally maintained dictionaries/enumerations as code systems, distinguishes code systems from value sets, and provides a local code-system URI example. Quoted Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Adding limited-scope prose to ValueSet would now reintroduce obsolete inline-code-system terminology; the current source already conveys the correct local-code-system model.
